rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran; all 36 spec and story criteria pass, and every candidate was checked against the source. Request-changes because of 3 blocking findings: two code-quality.md violations no automated gate enforces (the ~150-line resolveLayered(), and a missing JSDoc on an exported function) and an untested handleStatus wiring for the ticket's core fix. Of 8 findings, 5 are advisory; 0 deferred; 11 candidates dismissed (see code-review-dismissed.local.md).

findings.title: handleStatus wiring has no command-level test
findings.problem: No test runs the `codemie profile status` command. handleStatus now takes configDir, config and modelText from loadStatusConfig(), reads profiles, the active name and the local-config flag from configDir, and passes `model: modelText` to ProfileDisplay.formatStatus. model-override-parity.test.ts only calls loadStatusConfig() directly, and index.test.ts only calls formatStatus() directly with a hand-built identity.model. The only parseAsync call (index.test.ts:177) runs the list view.
findings.impact: If handleStatus stopped passing `model: modelText`, or went back to process.cwd() for listProfiles/getActiveProfileName/resolveIdentityDisplay, `codemie profile status` would again show the stored profile model or a different profile than the launcher uses. That is the exact bug this ticket fixes, and no test would fail. Consumer: `codemie profile status` via createStatusCommand.
findings.recommendation: Add a test in src/cli/commands/profile/__tests__/index.test.ts that runs createProfileCommand().parseAsync(['status'], { from: 'user' }) from a repo subfolder with CODEMIE_MODEL set (and a case with a <cwd>/.env). Assert that the printed Model line contains '<env model> (CODEMIE_MODEL from shell env overrides profile: <profile model>)' and that the active profile shown comes from the nearest .codemie.

findings.title: resolveLayered exceeds the 50-line function rule
findings.problem: code-quality.md Code Structure Guidelines require functions under 50 lines with one responsibility. The new ConfigLoader.resolveLayered() is about 150 lines. One body does defaults, profile selection, global/project/workspace layering, identity dropping, .env loading, env filtering under --profile, CLI overrides and model-resolution bookkeeping. eslint.config.mjs has no max-lines rule, so no automated gate enforces the limit.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality rule is unmet by a function this change introduces. That function is now the single merge path behind both load() and loadWithSources(), so every future config change lands in it.
findings.recommendation: Split resolveLayered() into named helpers: the identity/workspace step (around lines 259-281) and the --profile env filtering (around lines 294-339, which can become a loop over the protected keys). Leave resolveLayered() as the ordered sequence of apply() calls plus the model-resolution bookkeeping.

findings.title: resetModelOriginRecords export lacks JSDoc
findings.problem: code-quality.md Comments & Documentation requires 'JSDoc on all public APIs'. The exported resetModelOriginRecords() has none, unlike every other export in the module. No eslint jsdoc rule enforces it.
findings.impact: A documented code-quality rule is unmet on a newly exported function. It is used only by tests, and a reader of the module cannot tell that.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line JSDoc saying it clears the in-process .env and saved-pick records, for tests.

findings.title: Saved-pick recording in codemie-copilot untested
findings.problem: The 'saved' origin is tested only by calling recordSavedModelPick() by hand (model-override-parity.test.ts, model-origin.test.ts). No test loads bin/codemie-copilot.js, so nothing checks that applySavedModelIfNeeded records the pick after it sets CODEMIE_MODEL.
findings.impact: Narrow: a regression only changes label text. If the call were dropped or moved, the codemie-copilot banner would call a saved pick 'CODEMIE_MODEL from shell env' and no test would fail. The model in use is unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Move applySavedModelIfNeeded's model handling into a testable module, or add a test that, given a saved model.json and no --model/CODEMIE_MODEL, asserts resolveModelEnvOrigin() returns 'saved'.

findings.title: --show-sources subfolder wiring untested
findings.problem: No test runs `codemie profile status --show-sources`. handleStatusWithSources now passes findNearestConfigDir(cwd) as the config dir and cwd as envDir, but the existing tests call ConfigLoader.showWithSources(workingDir) directly with one directory.
findings.impact: Narrow: only the directory arguments are untested; the merge and the (.env) label are covered. If it went back to showWithSources() with no arguments, --show-sources run from a subfolder would disagree with plain status and the launcher, and no test would fail.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that runs the status command with --show-sources from a repo subfolder holding a .env with CODEMIE_MODEL. Assert '<value> (.env)' and that the profile comes from the parent repo's .codemie.

findings.title: ENV_LAYER_VARS duplicates loadFromEnv variable list
findings.problem: ENV_LAYER_VARS is a hand-written copy of the variable names loadFromEnv() reads, and nothing keeps the two in sync. Today they match (config.ts:724-756 reads exactly the listed variables).
findings.impact: No behaviour consequence today. If a later change adds a variable to loadFromEnv() but not to ENV_LAYER_VARS, a .env value for that key would always show as (env) in --show-sources.
findings.recommendation: Derive both from one table (key -> variable names) that loadFromEnv() also reads, or add a test asserting every key loadFromEnv() can return has an ENV_LAYER_VARS entry.

findings.title: Extra local config read on every load
findings.problem: Every load(), including the launch path, now calls loadLocalMultiProviderConfig(workingDir) only to label the tooling-workspace source. load() already reads that file through other calls (config.ts:168, 380, 428).
findings.impact: Minor: one more small JSON read per load and no user-visible effect. The read is needed only for --show-sources attribution.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the local multi-provider config already read in this pass, or let resolveIdentityFor() return the workspace scope it used, instead of reading the file again.

findings.title: Windows lowercase .env key mislabelled as shell
findings.problem: On Windows, loadDotenv uppercases names for its presence check, but recordDotenvValues stores each key as written in .env, and isFromDotenv('CODEMIE_MODEL') looks it up by exact case. A .env line such as `codemie_model=x` is still read by loadFromEnv, because the Windows environment is case-insensitive, but it is never matched as dotenv.
findings.impact: Narrow trigger: a lowercase or mixed-case variable name in .env on Windows. The banner and status then say 'CODEMIE_MODEL from shell env' and --show-sources prints (env) instead of (.env). Workaround: write the name in uppercase.
findings.recommendation: Record keys normalized the same way loadDotenv's presence check normalizes them (envKeyId(k)), and normalize the lookup key in isFromDotenv the same way. For example, recordDotenvValues(Object.fromEntries(entries.map(([k, v]) => [envKeyId(k), v]))) plus dotenvValues.get(envKeyId(key)), with envKeyId moved into model-origin.ts or passed in.
